# Results — Study 607 (Quarterly Refunding Shock)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
Treasury's Quarterly Refunding Announcement (QRA) moves the long end**; Aug/Nov 2023
supposedly turned QRA day into a first-tier macro event — tested on all **106 QRA dates
2000-02-02 → 2026-05-06** (hardcoded from the official TreasuryDirect auction records: the
mid-quarter refunding securities are announced *via* the refunding statement, so their
`announcementDate` is the QRA date; all 106 are Wednesdays, 08:30 ET) against ^TNX/^TYX
daily yield changes and TLT. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30**. Fingerprints:
^TNX `07c63093f8d2`, ^TYX `0f37876ddb3a`, TLT `ef0fdae90551`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Events | 106 QRA statement dates 2000→2026, derived once from TreasuryDirect TA_WS (`securities/search?type=Note`), hardcoded with source in [`data.py`](../quarterly_refunding_shock/data.py) |
| Tape | ^TNX 10Y yield (6,696 days, 1999-11-01 → 2026-06-26), ^TYX 30Y yield (same span), TLT total-return close (6,018 days, 2002-07-30 → 2026-06-30) — yfinance, cached |
| Decontamination | **37 of 106 QRA days (35%) are ALSO FOMC statement days** (both calendars pick early-Feb/May/Aug/Nov Wednesdays — 2023-11-01 included). Primary test uses the **69 FOMC-clean** QRA days vs a baseline of 5,936 sessions with no QRA-window day and no FOMC day |
| Execution / costs | announcement at 08:30 ET → the **day-0 close is the one execution lag** for the TLT legs; 2/5 bps one-way × 2 legs per event; ~4 events/yr |
| Survivorship | none — the full official announcement record + constant-maturity yield indices |

## Day-0 — does the 10Y move more on QRA day? (the Signal axis)

Events sit ~63 trading days apart, so event-day observations are serially uncorrelated and
the Welch *t* on |Δy| is the appropriate robust statistic (no overlapping windows — nothing
for HAC to fix). The placebo redraws 2,000 random same-size calendars from the baseline.

| set | n | day-0 \|Δy10\| | baseline \|Δy10\| | ratio | Welch *t* | signed Δy10 | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **FOMC-clean QRA days (primary)** | 69 | **3.86 bps** | 4.28 bps | **×0.90** | **−1.12** | +0.03 bps | +0.05 |
| all QRA days | 106 | 3.91 bps | 4.28 bps | ×0.91 | −1.18 | −0.30 bps | −0.61 |
| FOMC-overlap QRA days | 37 | 4.02 bps | 4.28 bps | ×0.94 | −0.48 | −0.91 bps | −1.08 |

- **Placebo:** observed 3.86 bps vs random-calendar mean 4.27 bps — **p = 0.823** (82% of
  random calendars beat the QRA calendar).
- **In-tape positive control:** the 175 FOMC-only statement days, pushed through the *same*
  pipeline, show |Δy10| **5.17 bps = ×1.21** the baseline, Welch *t* = **+2.24** — the
  method detects a genuine macro event on this very tape; it simply finds nothing on QRA
  day.
- **30Y (^TYX) robustness** — "the long end" proper: clean day-0 |Δy30| **4.37 bps** vs
  baseline 3.97 bps (×1.10), Welch *t* = **+0.73**; signed +0.10 bps (*t* = +0.13). Same
  verdict at the tenor the claim is actually about.

The 10Y moves **slightly less** on QRA day than on an ordinary day, and no signed drift
exists on the day. The announcement-day shock the 2023 folklore promises is **absent** on
26.5 years of tape.

## The event window [-1..+3] — and the jobs-report collision

Per-offset |Δy10| on the 69 clean QRA days vs the 4.28 bps baseline:

| offset | \|Δy10\| | Welch *t* | signed | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| −1 | 4.67 bps | +0.91 | −0.25 bps | −0.35 |
| **0** | **3.86 bps** | **−1.12** | +0.03 bps | +0.05 |
| +1 | 3.99 bps | −0.69 | −0.77 bps | −1.23 |
| **+2** | **6.42 bps** | **+4.10** | +2.17 bps | +2.41 |
| +3 | 3.49 bps | −1.72 | +0.48 bps | +0.77 |

The lone significant bump — day +2, Welch *t* = +4.10 — is **not a QRA aftershock**: QRA
lands on an early-month Wednesday, and the BLS Employment Situation lands on the **first
Friday** at 08:30 ET, which is day +2 of the window. **63 of 69 (91%)** clean-QRA day+2
sessions are first-Fridays; those alone average 6.62 bps, and **excluding them the day+2
excess vanishes** (4.30 bps, Welch *t* = **+0.01**, n = 6). The window's only signal
belongs to the jobs report, not to Treasury.

## Third axis — was 2023 a regime change, or two loud data points?

Each day's |Δy10| is normalised by the trailing 60-day mean |Δy10| (ending the day before),
so a 2023 QRA day is judged against 2023's own noise level. Eras split at 2023-01-01
(14 QRA days since; honest small-n).

| set | 2000–22 norm (n) | 2023+ norm (n) | Welch late-vs-early | drop Aug-2 + Nov-1 2023 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| all QRA days | 0.90× (92) | 1.17× (14) | *t* = **+1.21** | 1.20× (12), *t* = +1.16 |
| **FOMC-clean** | 0.95× (62) | **0.99× (7)** | *t* = **+0.10** | 1.07× (6), *t* = +0.26 |

Raw excess ratios vs each era's own baseline: early ×0.86, late ×1.23 (all QRA days);
early ×0.91, late ×0.82 (clean). Neither era's QRA days beat their own baseline (early
*t* = −1.39, late *t* = +0.97 all-days; −0.57 / +0.06 clean).

And the two storied days themselves, off the tape:

| date | event | Δy10 day-0 | note |
|---|---|--:|---|
| 2023-07-31 | borrowing estimate (+$274B surprise: $1,007B vs $733B) | **−1.0 bps** | the "shock" day the narrative starts from |
| 2023-08-02 | QRA statement (sizes up, first since 2021) | **+2.7 bps** | 0.51× its own era's noise; Fitch stripped the US AAA the evening before |
| 2023-10-30 | borrowing estimate ($776B, $76B below July's flag) | +3.0 bps | wrong sign for the "relief" story on the day |
| 2023-11-01 | QRA statement (long-end increases slowed) | **−8.6 bps** | **FOMC statement the same day at 14:00 ET** — inseparable on daily bars |

The Aug-2023 refunding **week** moved +9.1 bps and the Nov-2023 week −28.7 bps — real
moves, but spread over Fitch, the jobs report, and an FOMC, not concentrated at 08:30 on
QRA day. On FOMC-clean days the 2023+ era is **0.99×** its own noise — indistinguishable
from the 0.95× of 2000–2022 (*t* = +0.10), and dropping the two loud days *raises* the
late-era mean (they weren't even loud on day-0). **Two loud weeks, not a regime change.**

## Tradability — TLT after the announcement

Entry at the **day-0 close** (the one lag), exit 3 sessions later; ~4 events/yr; windows
non-overlapping. Baseline = 1,793 non-overlapping 3-day TLT windows outside events.

| leg | gross bps/event | *t* | net @ 2 bps 1-way | net @ 5 bps 1-way |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| unconditional long TLT (96 events) | **−14.3** | −0.89 | −18.3 (−73 bps/yr) | −24.3 (−97 bps/yr) |
| conditional (ride the day-0 sign) | **−21.3** | −1.33 | −25.3 (−102 bps/yr) | −31.3 (−126 bps/yr) |

Baseline 3-day windows average **+4.6 bps**; the post-QRA windows are (insignificantly)
*worse* than ordinary ones (Welch *t* = −1.15). Both legs lose money **before** costs.
(The conditional leg is short TLT about half the time; TLT borrow — ~50 bps/yr, ~0.4
bps per 3-day window — is not netted above because it can only deepen an already
negative leg.) There is nothing to deploy.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is faithful

Deterministic pseudo-QRA world (i.i.d. daily Δy, events every 63 sessions), knobs =
event-day vol multiplier + signed event-day mean. *(Machinery proof only — never market
evidence.)*

| planted | \|Δy\| ratio | Welch *t* | signed mean | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| vol ×1.0, mean 0 (null) | ×1.08 | +1.09 | −0.91 bps | −1.48 |
| **vol ×2.0**, mean 0 | ×2.17 | **+7.65** | −1.81 bps | −1.48 |
| vol ×1.0, **mean +4 bp** | ×1.19 | +2.20 | +3.09 bps | **+5.05** |

The null does not fire; a planted vol shock or signed drift lights up immediately. The
real-tape nulls are genuine absences, not blind instruments.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** On the 69 FOMC-clean QRA days the 10Y moves **×0.90** of an ordinary
  day (Welch *t* = −1.12; placebo p = 0.82); the 30Y is ×1.10 (*t* = +0.73); signed day-0
  drift is nil. The only significant window bump (day+2, *t* = +4.10) is the **jobs
  report** — 91% of those sessions are first-Fridays, and without them the excess is
  *t* = +0.01. No survivorship (full official record).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Both TLT legs are negative **gross** (−14.3 and −21.3
  bps/event) and worse net. Nothing survives costs because nothing exists before costs.
- **"2023 = regime change?" — BUSTED.** FOMC-clean 2023+ QRA days run **0.99×** their own
  era's noise vs 0.95× pre-2023 (Welch *t* = +0.10). Aug-2 2023 moved **+2.7 bps** (0.51×
  local noise, with Fitch in the tape); Nov-1 2023's −8.6 bps carries a **same-day FOMC**.
  The famous moves were refunding-**week** moves entangled with other catalysts — two loud
  weeks, not a new QRA-day regime.
